articles.title: Rust Belt Rising
articles.author: Rochester Red Star: News from Rochester DSA
articles.content_excerpt: by Hannah W. The first ever Rust Belt Rising conference was held on August 15th and 16th here in Rochester. This was organized by Workers Assembly of Rochester (WAR), an independent organization of local labor activists, including DSA members, union staffers and organizers. Local labor leaders, rank and file members and members of community organizations gathered to discuss and learn about the role of the labor movement in Rochester, and how we can move it to be more militant and left. Opening Keynote The opening keynote was a panel containing Colin, an organizer with the Teamsters Local 118, Christina, President of the Federation of Social Workers and Max from Buffalo DSA and Field Director for the Adam Bojak Campaign. articles.title: Disclosure Day and the Ultimate Other
articles.author: DSA Religion and Socialism Working Group
articles.content_excerpt: As someone with a space science background and a long-term interest in the search for extraterrestrial intelligence ( SETI ), I could not avoid the recent film on that topic, Disclosure Day . The film fits within the genre of UFO flicks dating back at least to the classic The Flying Saucer (1950) , the first film on the topic. The film’s release also coincides with recent testimonies of government officials claiming that the U.S. government is secretly studying and reverse-engineering extraterrestrial technology and the recent study by NASA on Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAPs). articles.title: The Canton–Hong Kong Strike Changed China’s History
articles.author: Promise Li
articles.content_excerpt: A century ago, workers in Hong Kong and Guangzhou — then generally known in English as Canton — waged one of the longest continuous general strikes in history. At the time, foreign powers such as Britain and Japan had carved China into spheres of influence. Wave after wave of students’ and workers’ movements struggled against this imperialist control, especially the May Fourth Movement of 1919. This anti-imperialist upsurge reached a fever pitch on May 30, 1925. That day, the police opened fire on students who were marching toward the British-controlled part of Shanghai to protest the murder of a Chinese worker at a Japanese-owned cotton factory during a recent strike. articles.title: Socialists Need Labor. And Labor Needs Socialists.
articles.author: Vivek Chibber
articles.content_excerpt: Unions have more public support than just about anything else in the United States, and yet their membership has cratered. This poses an immense challenge to left-wing politicians who won’t be able to enact lasting change without a robust labor movement beside them. On this latest episode of the Jacobin Radio podcast Confronting Capitalism , Vivek Chibber addresses the age-old question of whether unions are inherently political, the importance (and limits) of internal democracy within unions, and why socialists have always been at the heart of the labor movement. Confronting Capitalism with Vivek Chibber is produced by Catalyst: A Journal of Theory and Strategy and published by Jacobin . You can listen to the full episode here . articles.title: Zohran Mamdani Just Created an Office of Worker Power
articles.author: Zohran Mamdani
articles.content_excerpt: On Thursday, Mayor Zohran Mamdani signed an executive order creating the Mayor’s Office of Worker Power (MOWP), the nation’s first municipal agency built to help workers organize. Tony Perlstein will run the MOWP, reporting to Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice Julie Su. A former longshoreman and union organizer born and raised in New York, Perlstein served as an organizing director for the United Auto Workers, where he helped lead a national campaign to lift pay and protect jobs from automation. As part of its mandate, the MOWP will regularly bring union leaders and rank-and-file members together to discuss worker issues and organizing drives. articles.title: For Labor Day, $20 Print Subscriptions Worldwide
articles.content_excerpt: Labor Day isn’t the most exciting of holidays. It doesn’t quite have the verve or internationalism of May Day, and its meaning is overshadowed by important things like discounts on flat-screen TVs.But Labor Day was a real victory for the workers’ movement. As Tim Goulet writes in Jacobin, the holiday finds its roots in the most radical struggles of the nineteenth century. More than a decade before Grover Cleveland sanctioned a federal observance in 1894, Labor Day was marked by socialists and radical trade unionists.We might still prefer May Day, but hey, workers deserve at the very least two days to celebrate their contributions to society.Hopefully, we’re not mimicking the TV retailers too much, but we want to use the opportunity to share Jacobin with as many people as possible. articles.title: No, Seriously, Democratic Socialists Want to Abolish the Senate
articles.author: Rochester Red Star: News from Rochester DSA
articles.content_excerpt: by Gregory Lebens-Higgins On July 14, 2026, the national body of the Democratic Socialists of America released Workers Deserve More, a program outlining the organization’s goals and values. Workers Deserve More was drafted by a committee consisting of members of the National Political Committee, leaders of other national committees, and rank and file members following a process outlined by a resolution passed at DSA’s 2025 National Convention . Upon its release, Workers Deserve More received significant attention in mainstream media. The coverage has provided free advertising for DSA’s popular demands such as universal healthcare, improved working conditions, and replacing the two-party system with a multi-party democracy.
